    <h1 class="bok-title">The ML Systems Taxonomy</h1>
    <p class="bok-lede">A shared map of what an ML systems engineer needs to know. It is organized as the <strong>lifecycle</strong> that builds a system, the <strong>stack</strong> it runs on, and the <strong>qualities</strong> it is judged by, on shared <strong>foundations</strong>. Each subject has a code to cite, and each concept has a page showing what it affects and where MLSysBook teaches it. We built this taxonomy to organize the four volumes of <em>Machine Learning Systems</em> and share it here in case a common vocabulary is useful to the field. Additions and corrections are welcome <a href="https://github.com/harvard-edge/cs249r_book/issues/new?template=taxonomy_feedback.yml">on GitHub</a>.</p>

  <details class="bok-about">
    <summary>About this taxonomy: scope, method, tagging, and known gaps</summary>
    <div class="bok-about-body">
      <p>We developed this taxonomy to organize the four-volume <em>Machine Learning Systems</em> textbook series and share it openly so educators, researchers, and engineering teams can reuse or adapt it. No published, community-endorsed body of knowledge for ML systems existed when this draft was written. Courses split between a compute-stack tradition (deep learning systems) and a production tradition (ML systems design and MLOps). This taxonomy joins the two and adds what both tend to leave out: datacenter infrastructure, safety and assurance, sustainability, and agentic and embodied systems.</p>
      <p>Each concept has one home, the subject that owns its mechanism; other placements appear as related subjects. The taxonomy organizes knowledge for browsing and does not prescribe a course order or prerequisites. Relationships are editorial drafts, each with the condition under which it holds. Book links point to where MLSysBook teaches a subject; a missing link is unfinished alignment, not evidence that the books omit it.</p>
      <p>This is an editorial draft for expert review, not a claim of completeness, consensus, or demonstrated learning. Suggestions and corrections are welcome <a href="https://github.com/harvard-edge/cs249r_book/issues/new?template=taxonomy_feedback.yml">on GitHub</a>.</p>
      <div class="bok-known-gaps" id="bok-tagging"></div>
      <div class="bok-known-gaps" id="bok-gaps"></div>
      <p class="bok-method" id="bok-method"></p>
    </div>
  </details>
